issues.t: ABS module can short and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning at all. Some owners may see the ABS light come on or smell burning from the engine bay, even with the car parked and off.
issues.why: The anti-lock brake control unit (called the HECU) can short out inside. Because it stays powered, the short can start a fire in the engine bay whether the car is running or parked.
issues.next: Check your VIN for Kia recalls SC227 and SC284. Until the free fuse fix is done, Kia advises parking outdoors and away from buildings. If you smell burning or see smoke, get away from the car and call for help.

issues.t: Turbo oil feed line can leak and start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: Oil drips under the front of the car, a burning oil smell, or smoke from under the hood. There may be no warning light before it happens.
issues.why: The oil pipe and hose that feed the left turbocharger can wear out and leak. Oil landing on the hot turbo and exhaust can catch fire.
issues.next: Check your VIN for Kia recall SC300 and have the dealer replace the left turbo oil feed pipe for free. If you smell burning oil or see smoke, pull over and turn the engine off.

issues.t: Headlights flicker or shut off in Auto mode (recall)
issues.sym: On cars with LED headlights, the headlights flicker or go dark for a moment while you are driving, usually with the light switch set to AUTO.
issues.why: Over time the contacts inside the multi-function light switch build up electrical resistance, which confuses the switch's built-in electronics and interrupts power to the headlights.
issues.next: Check your VIN for Kia recall SC130. The dealer replaces the multi-function switch for free. Until then, watch the headlights closely at night and pull over safely if they go out.

issues.t: Harsh upshifts from worn transmission solenoids
issues.sym: A hard jolt when the 8-speed automatic shifts up through the middle gears (2nd to 3rd, 3rd to 4th or 4th to 5th), usually after the car has passed about 12,000 miles.
issues.why: Two shift solenoids inside the transmission can wear early. Kia released updated solenoids with an extra vent port, plus new shift software.
issues.next: Ask a Kia dealer about bulletin TSB TRA096. The fix is replacing the two solenoids, relearning the transmission and updating its software, not replacing the whole transmission.

issues.t: Rough downshift from 3rd to 2nd gear
issues.sym: A bump or clunk as the car slows down and the transmission drops from 3rd to 2nd gear, mostly in stop-and-go driving.
issues.why: On early-build 2015 cars the transmission computer's shift programming was not as smooth as it could be. Kia released improved shift software.
issues.next: Ask a Kia dealer to check whether service action SA174 (a transmission computer update) has been done. It is a software fix and takes about an hour.

issues.t: A/C stops cooling from a seized compressor
issues.sym: The A/C blows warm or only slightly cool air, or stops cooling completely. Sometimes the refrigerant has all leaked out.
issues.why: The A/C compressor can seize inside, or its casing can crack and lose all the refrigerant. Kia issued bulletins to help dealers spot a seized compressor and replace it.
issues.next: Have a shop check the A/C pressures. If the compressor is seized or cracked it needs to be replaced along with a new receiver-drier, then the system is evacuated and recharged.

issues.t: Hard to start or shut off from a broken start button
issues.sym: Pressing the Start/Stop button doesn't start the car, or the car is hard to turn off. The button may feel loose or broken.
issues.why: On early-build 2015 cars the cap inside the push-button start switch can break, so pressing the button doesn't register properly.
issues.next: Ask a Kia dealer about service action SA228. They inspect the button and replace the switch if the cap is broken.

issues.t: Unsteady engine speed on early V8 cars
issues.sym: Engine speed (RPM) may not hold steady, for example at idle.
issues.why: Some early 2015 V8 cars, built January to April 2014, left the factory without the latest engine computer software. Kia released an update to steady engine speed.
issues.next: Ask a Kia dealer to check for service action SA165 (an engine computer update). If the engine still runs rough after that, have it checked for a misfire or vacuum leak.

issues.t: Weak low-beam headlights
issues.sym: The low beams light up only a short distance ahead, so you need the high beams on dark roads. High beams work fine.
issues.why: Owners report the low-beam pattern is short and dim. Dealer re-aiming of the headlights often didn't solve it.
issues.next: Have the dealer check the headlight aim and the auto-leveling system, and make sure the bulbs or LED modules are working. Ask about warranty coverage if the car is still covered.

issues.t: Car pulls to one side
issues.sym: The car drifts or pulls to the left or right on a straight road, sometimes when nearly new.
issues.why: Owners report pulling on these years. Common causes are wheel alignment, uneven tire pressure or a tire problem.
issues.next: Check tire pressures first, then have a four-wheel alignment done. If it still pulls, ask the shop to swap the front tires side to side to see if a tire is causing it.

issues.t: Fog or moisture inside the headlights
issues.sym: A light haze or droplets on the inside of the headlight lens, often after rain or a car wash.
issues.why: Headlights breathe through vents, so some fogging is normal and should clear after the lights have been on for a while. Standing water or heavy droplets that won't clear point to a leak.
issues.next: Run the headlights with the engine on for up to 30 minutes. If the moisture stays or water pools inside, have a dealer inspect it; Kia's bulletin says a new headlight is not usually needed.

issues.t: Oily film on the brake calipers
issues.sym: An oily or wet-looking film on a brake caliper, which can look like a brake fluid leak.
issues.why: Kia found that extra assembly oil put on at the factory can show up on the calipers, so dealers inspect before replacing parts.
issues.next: Check that the brake fluid level is normal and the pedal feels firm. Have a shop confirm whether it's a real fluid leak or just assembly oil before replacing a caliper.

issues.t: Collision warning or smart cruise warning light
issues.sym: A warning light for forward collision assist or smart cruise control stays on, and those systems may turn off.
issues.why: The front radar sensor can be knocked out of alignment, or its mount may be loose or damaged, so the system can't see the road properly.
issues.next: Have a dealer inspect the radar sensor mounting and recalibrate it. Keep the sensor area on the front of the car clean of snow, ice and dirt.

issues.t: Front headrest hard to adjust
issues.sym: The front seat headrest is hard to raise or lower.
issues.why: On cars built March to September 2014, the module that moves the headrest up and down can be faulty.
issues.next: Ask a Kia dealer about service action SA177, which replaces the headrest elevator module.

issues.t: Navigation error message from the wrong SD card
issues.sym: The navigation screen shows an error message and maps don't load properly.
issues.why: The map SD card in the navigation unit doesn't match the head unit, which can happen on new cars or after the head unit has been replaced.
issues.next: Have a Kia dealer check and exchange the navigation SD card. Don't buy an aftermarket card.

issues.t: UVO connected services not working
issues.sym: UVO features such as remote start from the app, vehicle status or roadside help don't work, even on a new car.
issues.why: The UVO telematics system may not be activated or communicating properly.
issues.next: Have a Kia dealer check the UVO activation and the head unit software. Make sure the account and app are set up correctly.

issues.t: UVO services dead until the head unit is reset
issues.sym: Connected UVO services don't work on the new-generation car.
issues.why: On cars built July to September 2018, the audio/navigation (AVN) unit needed a factory reset to get UVO working.
issues.next: Ask a Kia dealer about service action SA376, which is a factory reset of the head unit.

issues.t: Transmission cooler line connection can come loose
issues.sym: Red transmission fluid drips under the car, or the transmission starts slipping or shifting oddly if fluid is lost.
issues.why: On cars built August to November 2018, the quick-connect fittings on the transmission cooler lines may not be fully seated.
issues.next: Ask a Kia dealer about service action SA368, an inspection of the cooler hoses. If you see fluid leaking, stop driving and have it checked, because low fluid can damage the transmission.

issues.t: Squeak from the turbo wastegate when accelerating
issues.sym: An odd squeaking or rattling noise when you press the gas pedal.
issues.why: A dealer traced this to the turbocharger wastegate rods squeaking from heat. It can come back after a repair.
issues.next: Have a dealer confirm the noise is from the wastegate linkage and not a leak or loose heat shield. Ask about warranty coverage while the car is covered.

issues.t: Battery drains when devices are left plugged in
issues.sym: The car is slow to crank or won't start after sitting, with phones, dashcams or other devices left plugged in.
issues.why: Devices left connected can keep drawing power after the car is off and run down the 12-volt battery.
issues.next: Unplug devices when you park, and have the battery tested. If it still drains, a shop can measure the battery drain with everything off.

issues.t: Sunglass holder door won't latch
issues.sym: The overhead sunglass holder door won't stay closed and may rattle.
issues.why: The latch on the sunglass door in the overhead console can stop working.
issues.next: Ask a dealer about bulletin TSB BOD314, which repairs the overhead console and latch.

issues.t: Radio presets erased after a reboot
issues.sym: Saved radio stations disappear after the screen or head unit restarts.
issues.why: A software problem in the Premium Gen 2.0 head unit on 2020 cars can erase presets during a reboot.
issues.next: Ask a Kia dealer about service action SA443, a free head unit software update.

issues.t: Radio won't respond to the button or screen
issues.sym: Pressing the RADIO button or icon does nothing, so you can't switch to AM, FM or SiriusXM.
issues.why: A software problem in the wide-screen audio/navigation unit.
issues.next: Ask a dealer for the head unit software update in bulletin TSB ELE303.
